newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Maya Angelou, new UNICEF ambassador, gives awards.
newsitem.headline: Maya Angelou, new UNICEF ambassador, gives awards.

text.p: Maya Angelou, poet, author and actress, on Tuesday was named American Ambassador to UNICEF, the U.N. Children's Fund.

"If the child is white, it's your child, if the child is black, that is your child, if the child is Spanish-speaking or Asian or native-American, that is your child. To understand that, to have the courage to understand that, means that one is liberated," she said at the UNICEF lunch after singing an English lullaby adapted by slaves in the United States.

Angelou then presided over a ceremony where Broadway actress Rachel York presented prizes to women from Somalia, Peru and India singled out for achievement by the U.N. Development Fund for Women (UNIFEM), which specializes in grass roots projects in developing countries.
-- Iida, a group mobilizing women from various clans to advocate peace among warring factions in Somalia and providing housing and training for those displaced by the war.
-- Los Molineras, the Women Millers, a group of 10 women who run a rural food business in Peru's Andean region by making flour from local grains.

-- India's Center for Social research which trains women leaders and counsels on health care, jobs and legal rights. The award was accepted by Rekha Dubey, a leader in the group who was an abused wife at 14 and regained custody of her children and property.
York gave the prizes on behalf of British actress Julie Andrews, a UNIFEM goodwill ambassador.
